subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What request-scoped no-side-effects contract should OpenClaw expose for global agent tool dry-run across CLI, Gateway/embedded runs, built-in/plugin/client tools, direct tool invocation, and hooks?
rationale: This feature would become a user-trusted safety boundary, and current source shows multiple execution surfaces that a narrow adapter/global flag would not safely cover.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, hook, and output behavior.

options.title: Fold into workflow modes
options.body: Keep this open but block implementation until Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent mode defines the shared preview vocabulary and guarantees.

options.title: Keep only scoped dry-runs
options.body: Reject a global mode if maintainers decide it is too easy to confuse with sandboxing, and continue improving command-specific preview paths instead.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, hook, and output behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the adapter and hook execution contract points to this person, and the unresolved choice is a product/security boundary rather than a mechanical code repair.
